problem: Consider the elliptic paraboloid $y+1=\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{5}+\frac{(z-2)^{2}}{3}.$ Which of the following gives its axis of symmetry, written as an intersection of two planes?
worked_solution:
First, we write our equation as 

$$
y-(-1)=\frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{5}+\frac{(z-2)^{2}}{3}.
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic paraboloid oriented along the $y$-axis that has its vertex at $(-4,-1,2).$
 Since it is oriented along the $y$-axis, we conclude that its axis of symmetry is parallel to the $y$-axis.

The axis of symmetry should pass through the vertex of the paraboloid. Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry can be written as an intersection of two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-4 \\ z=2\end{aligned}
$$
